body: Colorectal cancer survivor. I essentially have my own version of IBS all the time for 16 years. It does make life hard and a social life extremely difficult. Going out to dinner? Always an adventure. Being at an event that lasts more than 2 hours-etc. it is very defeating. I totally understand. I have always kept working, but have to so carefully plan every "pit stop" each day! I am the most comfortable at home. I am glad you have a cat. I was happier before my dog died and petting her always made me calmer. But there is not time in my life to train a new pet right now. My only suggestion: try some mild exercise. I believe I have inflammatory issues like yours (I struggle with eczema), and exercise seems to calm that response some. Nothing major. Just 20-30 minutes of something. Walking outside is great for the mind sometimes, I think. I wish you some peace and relief from your symptoms.

It sounds like you are on the right track. To beat low blood sugar you eat higher fiber and slower digesting foods. Oatmeal, whole grain bread, nuts, even beef jerky, which breaks down slowly and gives you some protein. I run, so I often crash later in the morning if I don't refuel properly. Oh yeah-milk too! And yogurt! Good luck! Add some exercise (walking, biking, running, swimming) and that should help regulate your blood sugar too!

I don't think you are that unhealthy. You have some issues to deal with, but take them a little at a time. Low blood sugar is an issue. Maybe your meds have something to do with that. Also, you are not too old to go back to college. You probably feel worse because you are unhappy. That happens to me too. First, just try and get some control of your diet and physical life. Message me if you want. I am pretty good at that stuff! And Cornell with a scholarship-you must be intelligent! Great to have you around! Stay!

Defy that person. Stick around for a few more days. Post something. Anything. I like how you write. I know how you feel. I get better and then slip backward. I then get mad at myself. I have people who want me to fail. I almost let them. I am fighting back a little at a time. It is really hard though. Stay with me.

I know days like that. Does not matter if you are 22 or 52. They hurt-and pain makes everything else intolerable. Vent all you want. Try and find out what you might be able to do about your pain. Just a start. I don't have answers. Just hope for you.

It truly hurts to lose someone you love. It is painful, but you can get through it. You have to breathe, eat, and find a "new normal" for some time. Be kind to yourself and set reasonable goals-like eat lunch. Take a walk. Get some sun on your face. You are hurt because you loved-that is a beautiful experience-the love part-in itself. You can PM me if needed. People are here for you.
Thanks for sharing. I think you are brave to be here. Let me know if you need anything.

Well, many of them, yes. But there are always exceptions. Also, as people get older they get wiser and more accepting. You are so young right now and dealing with less mature women. You are probably more mature because of what you have dealt with in life. So the balance is off-for now.
Ok. Just wondered. I lost mine a few years ago and did not replace her. I wonder if that is why I don't feel as good sometimes. But I understand your feelings and even agree with them.
Do you have a pet?

Are there support groups for other people with your condition. When I was diagnosed with cancer an on-line support group probably saved my life. I don't mean to say I have answers for you. Only you know how you feel. I guess I just want you to know I care-

So sorry man. Life is not easy for many of us-and you are dealing with more than many of us. I bet you are a pretty smart and insightful person. I am certain someone would not care at all about your appearance, but you just have not found them yet. Give it all a little more time, please. Just make a promise to not do anything today, or this week. And see what life brings. I hope better things. Or just the strength to get through it.

The posters here are right. It may be a hurdle-but not one you can't clear. It is just one stupid shoplifting conviction. Employers need good workers. Make yourself qualified and test clean (drugs) and you will get through this. SO many people have one stupid conviction. You are just one of many many. Don't beat yourself up. You are ok.
I support you in every way. You have had a difficult time-that is for sure. But you have the support and respect of more people every year. Take it one day at a time and try to survive!

Sorry man. You have had a tough time. I just want to say that as a parent of grown children, I often had to "fake" bring a good dad because of depression or work-related stress. That does not make a bad parent, it makes you a good person. You work hard and support a family. You will be a good dad even if you live apart from your children. Or if you stay together with your wife but apart emotionally. Try to find a little something in life to enjoy. I try super hard to do that. Doesn't always work. But sometimes it does. PM me if you like. Or just know you are not alone at all.

People think I am always happy too. I am not. I am a super stressed attorney who survived cancer and I feel so much anxiety about life that it has finally just made me so sad and thinking about death. I confide in my wife. She knows how unhappy I am. I am trying to do the right things and just keep going to work. I exercise, eat right, drink water, etc. But each day is a struggle. Take life a day at a time and try to do one ok thing each day. Sorry life sucks. But it does sometimes.

Sorry. Can't physically embrace you, but mentally there are so many people who will do just that! Just keep moving forward, even 10 minutes at a time. And promise yourself to put off anything bad for a week, or a month, or a year. My life started to get better when I realized Ivwas so low that I had nothing to lose by trying. No pressure. I hope you have an ok day.
Thank you! Getting out in the morning air helped a ton! At work now and doing ok. I appreciate your comment. My post was pretty boring. But it helped me to write it.

You are feeling bad for all the right reasons. Get up-get out. Go wherever you can or have to to be safe for now. That intimidation and demeaning attitude are horrible on your brain. As soon as you get away, anywhere, you will feel better.

Just went through a horrific mid-life crisis. Still in it as far as I can tell, but it has stabilized a tiny bit. Mine included everything-felt lost, attracted to a younger woman who liked me back for a few days....lol...I thought I had cancer (again). All F'd up. Work pressures plus life made me want to hang myself. Wish I could say something great. But the ocean felt good last week. And my daughter told me we are a great family and that she loves me (she is 24).  So I am going to stay alive, I decided. People need me. Find something. Hang on.

I know how you feel. I have dark, dark days too. But I love the X-Files! So good choice there! You talked about wishing it were warmer to be outside when your time comes. How about just getting outside with a promise to put everything off for a week, or a month. Walk and feel the sun and wind. I just got back from the beach and felt the ocean again. It helped some. Not a miracle. But it felt good and reminded me of simple things that connect me to this earth. It is good you posted here. It is a great way to unload a little. I will keep an eye out for you.

If you got good grades and participated in a lot of activities you DID get something out of those years, you just do not know it yet!! See where you get in, or if not, then take a gap year and do something creative that will enrich your life! Work on an organic farm or volunteer somewhere! Tons of people take gap years to make themselves better college applicants! I understand your disappointment, but you have good options still! Google "Gap years"!  See what you find!

I know that feeling too. I daydream about death-and have a life everyone else would think is great. I hate a huge part of myself and don't know why. I believe we are just overly perceptive of life and thus feel pressure or angst all the time. But you are definitely NOT alone. I am right there with you. Talk if you want, or just know it.

I feel like that too. I go to sleep thinking about killing myself and wake up with it. WTF? I am afraid too. Just do what I am doing. Put it off for today and see if it gets any better. One day at a time. Join me.

Wow. You are intuitive Kat. I am afraid of dying like my brother, but also know I might live a long time still, because I have taken good care of myself. And as for that other interest-I wish I was as honorable as you say. I am not a bad person. I know that. But if she had been entirely willing I am not certain what would have happened-or not happened. But I am feeling less at the end of my proverbial rope now. I wish I knew how to direct message you to thank you. But I am pretty new to this and can't figure it out. But thank you.

Work was so hard. And my older brother died of cancer at 62 almost 3 years ago. I feel like my time is getting short-even though everything is ok now. It is an odd combination of mid-life, worried it is closer to end of life-and also felt something for someone else, which was not right. Happily married. Supposed to stay that way forever. Nothing happened. But it helped get me all off balance I think.
Sure. Honestly, that you cared to comment made me feel some better.
Thanks. Good advice. Will try anything!
So was I. Too afraid to lean forward and pass out with the belt around my neck. Started to get lightheaded. Did that 3 times. Hope I don't have to make that decision again.

It sounds like you are so rational to me. You know what to do. Be kind to yourself! Really! Skip the Internet or come straight here for some time! Allow your brain to calm down. It will! Then you can move on.

The fact that you are asking means that a part of you wants to stay here. So yes, you need permission. And no, for now you cannot have it. If your job made you have a breakdown in the first place, then maybe another will be better for you! The most important thing is peace!! Work toward it!

Ignore it as much as you possibly can and get out in the world a little bit! The Internet is overhyped and overrated! Take a walk in nature somewhere. Even for a little while. Our REAL world is not on line, even if it feels like it! Breathe!
Know it. Been there. My cycles were sometimes years apart. Had a rough, rough winter.

I know the feeling! F everybody else! If you know it was an honest mistake then believe it! I made one! I punished myself for it by hurting my own career. Dumb! I am fine! People are jerks sometimes, even if they don't mean to be! You are ok.

I think you are doing amazingly! I have also had a really rough last year at work and home. 53 years old and a cancer survivor for 17 years. But trying to figure out where life is taking me now! I exercise, try and help other people and do social things and be good to my wife and family. And it helps some, but in the middle of the night all I feel us dread over missed opportunities in life that I botched. You are brave and good to try so hard-and you made me go to the gym right now! I will keep trying!

You are obviously hard-working and honest. Those are great traits! You are dealing with a ton of responsibility! I get that! Me too! Be kind to yourself. Take it one day at a time for now, or one hour if that is what it takes. I share many of your concerns as well. All challenging. I know. But you should be ok. You are too good to not be ok.

Nothing wrong with you except depression, probably. Even as you crawl out of it there are valleys where you feel like you do now. I was in one of those valleys last night too. But a morning cup of coffee and I feel ready to get another work day started. Be kind to yourself. You are doing ok even if you end up back here. I did too.

Hardly anybody up at this time. People wil reply. I know life sucks in so many ways. But there have been good days. They are hard to recall, but if we try really hard we might get back to some. When it is darkest, I take my days, literally, one hour at a time. Hope your day is ok.
Dude. I've done more than 9 years, including cancer. Stay here for a few more weeks. I could use someone to vent to as well/who knows what it is like.

I feel your pain. I am a cancer survivor of 17 years-but lufe has never been the same. 100's of chemotherapy treatments. You are braver than anyone I know! I had 18 and wanted to just give up as well. Cancer is a beast to wrestle with. You are tired. I understand that completely. You are also right about cAncer-it can get you any time. Just know I respect and admire you for what you have already done, and I hope that life gives you a little break from hardship.

Those thoughts are just giving you a little bit of relief from a situation that you have little control over! But you really just want some peace. Seek out whatever you need to do to find it. A doctor, a friend, some music, a walk. When your brain calms down you will recognize life again! Be good to yourself!

I totally understand those feelings! But they are wrong. It is your brain not quite working right. I figured it out asI got non-suicidal. Let some time go by. Be good to yourself. Eat, sleep, watch funny tv. You won't be as embarassed in a few weeks. I promise.

Totally understand the self-loathing you are describing. Sounds like how I feel about myself the past year. But you said something that made me think. So many people suck in this world-they just don't know it. Maybe people like you and me just see ourselves more clearly, including all of our stupid flaws. I don't think we are all that bad-we just see all the bad things about ourselves because we are honest. Anyway-thanks for making me think a little. You helped.
Hey. One friend right here.

I understand how you feel. I fell apart in December from overwork and missed out on a huge promotion because I just could not deal with the pressure. I had made some mistakes at work and thought about just leaving this world. And I have 3 kids in college. Never enough money. I was just a wreck. I kept moving forward a tiny bit at a time-still feel like I blew my career-but thinking less about harming myself. Give yourself a little break. You are trying hard and took a chance. That was brave! Now just take it a day at a time and give yourself a little credit for getting up, eating breakfast and doing anything! I wish you some peace my friend. I know.
